explanation: The A98G mutation removes a methyl side chain at position 98, creating a localized cavity within the fingers-palm subdomain approximately 5.6 Ångströms from etravirine. This loss of van der Waals packing density weakens the overall conformational stability of the NNRTI-binding pocket environment, as the surrounding protein scaffold loses hydrophobic contacts that normally constrain the ligand-binding geometry. Although the mutation does not directly contact etravirine, the reduced bulk destabilizes the protein backbone and side-chain orientations that position critical residues for optimal inhibitor engagement, resulting in modest but reproducible loss of binding affinity.
